page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Powered by custom 64-bit ARMv9 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors running at a sustained 2.8 GHz clock speed, this instance provides 64 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core. It is configured with 128 GB of DDR memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Hardware provisioning includes 3,800 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD local instance storage and 30 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark analysis shows strong multi-threaded and memory-intensive processing capacity. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 459.25 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput achieved 121.97 GB/sec. Parallel operations demonstrate strength in key-value store benchmarks, recording 133.11 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations alongside elevated Clang compilation scores. Conversely, single-core benchmarks remain in average performance bands, establishing that compute effectiveness is heavily tied to multi-core workload distribution.

From a system design standpoint, the instance delivers efficient compute and IOPS density by bundling 3,800 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity directly to the physical host, avoiding network storage latency for persistent cache or database layers. The c8gd.16xlarge is fit for concurrent web serving, distributed key-value databases, multi-threaded software build pipelines, batch data transformations, and containerized microservice deployments.
